sovereign

/SOV-rin/ - the stress falls on SOV · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Sovereign means having absolute authority in a certain realm.

The abbey on the lake has been sovereign for six centuries, minting its own coins and answering to no crown.

Example

The tribal nation's court sits a mile from the county courthouse, but the two are not neighbors in law: within the reservation the nation is sovereign, issuing its own license plates, running its own police, and trying its own cases under laws its own council writes.

Sovereign is stronger than 'independent' or 'self-governing': it means the authority is absolute within its realm — final say, with no outside power above it whose approval is ever required.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

independent: Independent means standing free of outside control, in fact or in law — an independent nation, an independent auditor. It says nobody runs your affairs; it does not say you hold the final word. Sovereign adds exactly that: absolute authority within a realm, with no last resort above it.

supreme: Supreme means highest-ranked: nothing inside the system outranks it, as a supreme court outranks every lower bench. But supreme power still lives inside a system that created it and could redraw its charter. Sovereign authority answers to nothing above it at all, inside the system or beyond.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dependent: relying on another power's support or say-so

beholden: owing loyalty or favors to someone above

Where it sits · how far above outside control it stands

free → autonomous → sovereign

free vs. sovereign: Free is the loosest word on this ladder — a person, a press, or a market can be free while still living under someone else's laws, a ceiling sovereign never accepts.

autonomous vs. sovereign: Autonomous already means self-governing, yet an autonomous region still sits inside a larger state that could, in the last resort, overrule it; sovereign closes that door — above a sovereign power there is nobody, which is why the ladder ends on it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — sovereign: above all others (worn down from Latin super, 'above')

Put it together: Sovereign wears a mask: Latin superanus — 'standing above' — slid through Old French soverain, and English scribes respelled its tail as -reign because a sovereign reigns. The g is a folk-etymology stowaway; the real root is super, 'above,' which is the whole meaning: the authority above which there is none.

Use the root in a new word: supreme: The supreme court's ruling ended the appeals; no higher bench exists to hear the case again.

Word Building

Word Choice

formal / constitutional

Sovereign is the constitution-writer's word: use it when authority is absolute within a realm and answers to nothing above it — a sovereign nation, sovereign control. Autonomous, its nearest neighbor, self-governs inside something larger; keep the two straight by asking who could overrule. This unit's potentate is sovereign power worn by one person.
